documents.source_category: Interim Financial Statements for the Quarter ended 30th June 2026

financials_interim.notes: Dialog Finance PLC (CALF) is a licensed finance company (NBFI), a subsidiary of Dialog Axiata PLC (99.05% owner). This filing presents a SINGLE set of statements (Company only, no subsidiaries to consolidate), so basis is recorded as GROUP by this project's convention for single-entity filings. Period entered is the SIX MONTHS ENDED 30 JUNE 2026 (H1 2026) -- the filing's own primary/certified period (title page: 'Condensed Interim Financial Statements for the Six Months Ended 30 June 2026'); the filing also discloses a three-months-ended-30-June column but the six-month cumulative figures are used here as the official period. Mapped per this project's NBFI convention (matches CDB/LOFC precedent): revenue = 'Total operating income' (1,604,419 = Net interest income 923,749 + Fee & commission income 650,822 + Net trading loss (813) + Other operating income 30,661) -- this line already nets out Interest expense (340,156) via Net Interest Income, so cost_of_sales/gross_profit/finance_costs/finance_income are left blank to avoid double-counting the interest expense. operating_profit = 'Operating Profit before taxes on financial services' (361,345), the company's own subtotal. Per the AAF-precedent two-tier tax convention: 'Taxes on financial services' (115,253, the VAT-FS-equivalent levy) sits between operating_profit and profit_before_tax and is NOT captured in tax_expense (no schema field for it) -- profit_before_tax is set to the filing's own 'Profit before tax for the period' (246,092, i.e. AFTER the taxes-on-financial-services deduction), and tax_expense = 'Income tax expense' only (99,221). Ties exactly: 246,092 - 99,221 = 146,871 = disclosed 'Profit for the period'. depreciation_amortization = 57,751 (Depreciation and amortization line in the P&L). Balance sheet: current_assets/current_liabilities/inventory/trade_receivables/trade_payables left blank per NBFI convention -- liquidity-ordered SOFP, no current/non-current split, and 'Financial assets at amortised cost - loans and advances' (10,500,237) is the core lending book, not a trade receivable. short_term_borrowings = 'Financial liabilities at amortised cost - due to banks' (2,012,904); no debenture/subordinated-debt line disclosed so long_term_borrowings is left blank. 'Financial liabilities at amortised cost - due to customers' (7,648,952, deposit funding) is deliberately EXCLUDED from borrowings per project convention -- customer deposits, not debt. Lease liabilities (104,069) also excluded, consistent with prior NBFI entries this project. total_assets (13,705,012) = total_liabilities (10,795,253) + total_equity (2,909,759) exactly. shares_in_issue = 117,399,866 (Note 6, Twenty largest shareholders total) -- cross-checked against EPS: 146,871k / 117,399,866 = Rs.1.2513, ties to disclosed EPS Rs.1.25. Cash flow figures are the six-month cumulative (H1 2026 vs H1 2025), consistent comparative basis (unlike some NBFI filings this project has seen where the cash-flow comparative is a full year). capex = 'Acquisition of property plant and equipment and intangible assets' (158,772, single combined line, no separate PPE/intangible split in the cash flow statement). KEY DRIVER: turnaround was driven by Device Financing and payments-business fee income -- Fee and commission income rose 72% YoY to Rs.650.8m (H1 2026) from Rs.379.2m (H1 2025), the single largest contributor to the 66.9% rise in Total operating income (Rs.1,604.4m vs Rs.961.4m), per the company's own financial review on page 2 and the segmental note (MSME segment net fee & commission income 187,367 up from 137,573; Consumer segment 463,455 up from 241,635).

interim_updates.note_text: Dialog Finance PLC (CALF), the Dialog Axiata-owned device-financing/consumer NBFI, delivered a sharp YoY turnaround for H1 2026 (six months ended 30 June 2026): Total operating income rose 66.9% to Rs.1,604.42mn from Rs.961.40mn in H1 2025, and Profit for the period grew 547% to Rs.146.87mn from Rs.22.68mn -- EPS rose to Rs.1.25 from Rs.0.19. The single largest driver is Fee and commission income, up 72.7% YoY to Rs.650.82mn (H1 2025: Rs.379.21mn) -- per the segmental note this is led by the Consumer segment (net fee & commission income Rs.463.46mn, up from Rs.241.64mn) with the MSME segment also contributing (Rs.187.37mn, up from Rs.137.57mn), consistent with device-financing and payments-business volume growth. Net interest income grew a more modest 64.0% to Rs.923.75mn as Interest income grew 71.4% to Rs.1,263.91mn against Interest expense growth of 95.1% to Rs.340.16mn (interest expense growing faster than interest income off a smaller base -- a funding-cost pressure worth watching even though NII still expanded in absolute terms). Impairment charges and other losses rose 79.7% YoY to Rs.186.63mn (H1 2025: Rs.103.87mn), a genuine credit-cost increase that partly offset the income growth but was outweighed by it -- Net operating income still grew 65.4% to Rs.1,417.79mn. Operating expenses also rose broadly in line with volume growth: Personnel expenses +48.3% to Rs.341.65mn, Depreciation and amortisation +66.2% to Rs.57.75mn, Other expenses +44.1% to Rs.657.04mn. Operating profit before taxes on financial services rose 164.8% to Rs.361.35mn (H1 2025: Rs.136.44mn). Taxes on financial services (the VAT-FS-equivalent levy sitting between operating profit and PBT) rose 85.3% to Rs.115.25mn, and Profit before tax rose 231.6% to Rs.246.09mn; Income tax expense rose a comparatively smaller 92.6% to Rs.99.22mn, so post-tax profit growth (547%) outpaced pre-tax profit growth (232%) because the H1 2025 base carried a disproportionately heavy tax charge relative to its thin pretax profit. Operating margin improved to 22.5% from 14.2% and net margin to 9.1% from 2.4%, both a genuine margin expansion, not merely a low-base effect, since the absolute profit increase (Rs.124.19mn) is large relative to the revenue base.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is CALF's first financial_statements/interim_updates entry in this DB (no closer prior quarter -- e.g. Q1 2026 alone -- has been separately collected; the filing's own three-months-ended-30-June column was not entered into financial_statements, only the six-month cumulative column, per this project's period-selection convention, so a true QoQ vs Q1 2026 cannot be derived from data already in the DB). Genuine filing-level gaps: (1) the funding-cost pressure implied by interest expense growing faster than interest income (95.1% vs 71.4%) is not explained qualitatively in the filing (e.g. no commentary on rate resets or funding-mix shift); (2) 'Taxes on financial services' (VAT-FS-equivalent, Rs.115.25mn this period) has no dedicated schema field and sits embedded between operating_profit and profit_before_tax -- flagged again here for clarity since it affects how the operating_profit-to-PBT bridge should be read; (3) the filing does not break out impairment charges by loan-book segment (MSME vs Consumer), so the 79.7% YoY impairment increase cannot be attributed to a specific segment from this document alone.
interim_updates.takeaway: CALF's H1 2026 turnaround is a genuine, broad-based operational improvement rather than a one-off item: Fee and commission income growth of 72.7% (Rs.650.82mn vs Rs.379.21mn), concentrated in the Consumer device-financing segment, is the dominant driver of the 66.9% revenue increase, and both operating margin (22.5% vs 14.2%) and net margin (9.1% vs 2.4%) expanded meaningfully. The main offsetting factor to watch is credit quality -- impairment charges rose 79.7% YoY to Rs.186.63mn -- and funding costs, with interest expense (+95.1%) outpacing interest income growth (+71.4%); neither has yet reversed the profit trajectory but both bear monitoring as the loan book scales further.

operational_highlights: Total operating income Rs.1,604.42mn, +66.9% YoY (H1 2025: Rs.961.40mn); Operating profit before taxes on financial services Rs.361.35mn, +164.8% YoY; Profit before tax Rs.246.09mn, +231.6% YoY; Profit for the period Rs.146.87mn, +547% YoY; EPS Rs.1.25 (H1 2025: Rs.0.19).

Fee and commission income +72.7% YoY to Rs.650.82mn (H1 2025: Rs.379.21mn) -- Consumer segment net fee & commission income Rs.463.46mn (up from Rs.241.64mn), MSME segment Rs.187.37mn (up from Rs.137.57mn).
Impairment charges and other losses +79.7% YoY to Rs.186.63mn (H1 2025: Rs.103.87mn); Net operating income still grew 65.4% to Rs.1,417.79mn despite the higher credit cost.
Net interest income +64.0% YoY to Rs.923.75mn; Interest income +71.4% to Rs.1,263.91mn vs Interest expense +95.1% to Rs.340.16mn -- funding cost growing faster than asset yield.
Operating margin improved to 22.5% from 14.2%; Net margin improved to 9.1% from 2.4%.
key_drivers: Fee and commission income growth of 72.7% YoY (Rs.650.82mn vs Rs.379.21mn), led by the Consumer segment (Rs.463.46mn vs Rs.241.64mn), is the single largest driver of the 66.9% rise in Total operating income and the resulting profit turnaround.
Impairment charges and other losses rose 79.7% YoY to Rs.186.63mn, a genuine and rising credit cost that partially offset (but did not reverse) the income growth.
Interest expense (+95.1% to Rs.340.16mn) grew faster than Interest income (+71.4% to Rs.1,263.91mn), a funding-cost pressure embedded within the otherwise-improving Net interest income line.
